---
title: "varslice"
subtitle: "Slicing gridded netCDF variables in space and time"
---

## Overview

`varslice` loads and slices gridded variables (up to four dimensions: `x`, `y`,
`z`, `time`) out of one or more netCDF files. It is the gridded cousin of the
lightweight [series](series.qmd) module: where `series` handles 0-D time series,
`varslice` handles full spatial fields that evolve over time.

The problem it solves is reading a *slice* of a large field without holding the
whole thing in memory or writing bespoke `nc_read` calls at every call site:

- **Time slicing** — given a target time (or time range), it reads only the
  required timesteps from disk and reduces them to the requested output via a
  configurable `slice_method` (exact match, range, interpolation, extrapolation,
  or a range statistic such as mean/min/max/standard deviation).
- **Sub-annual (subgrid) time** — a variable may carry a fractional sub-axis
  (e.g. 12 monthly values per year). `varslice` builds the sub-annual time axis
  and lets a range statistic repeat over it (e.g. produce a 12-month climatology
  by applying a mean to every 12th index).
- **Multi-file matching** — a single `filename` may be a glob pattern spanning
  many files; `varslice` expands it, concatenates the time dimension across
  files, and reads a contiguous span transparently.
- **Unit handling** — an input variable is rescaled on read via `unit_scale`
  and `unit_offset`, with missing values preserved.

The variable is configured once (from a namelist or from arguments), then
updated repeatedly to whatever time the calling model currently needs.

## Derived types

### `varslice_param_class`

Static configuration for one variable, mostly loaded from the namelist.

| Component | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `filename` | `character(len=1024)` | Source file or glob pattern (may contain `{domain}` / `{grid_name}`) |
| `filenames(:)` | `character(len=1024)`, alloc. | Expanded list of matching files |
| `name` | `character(len=56)` | netCDF variable name |
| `units_in` | `character(len=56)` | Units in the file (metadata) |
| `units_out` | `character(len=56)` | Units after scaling (metadata) |
| `unit_scale` | `real(wp)` | Multiplicative factor applied on read |
| `unit_offset` | `real(wp)` | Additive offset applied on read |
| `with_time` | `logical` | Whether the variable has a time dimension |
| `with_time_sub` | `logical` | Whether a sub-annual axis is used (derived from `time_par(4)`) |
| `ndim` | `integer` | Number of dimensions of the variable (set on init) |
| `time_par(4)` | `real(dp)` | Time-axis definition `[x0, x1, dx, n_sub]` |
| `mode` | `character(len=16)` | What the variable is, resolved at init: `static`, `clim` (a cycle without years) or `transient` |
| `time_ref` | `real(dp)` | Calendar year of time zero of the caller's clock (default 0) |
| `time_from_file` | `logical` | The time axis is read from the file (`time(1) < 0` or no `time` key) |
| `time_units`, `calendar` | `character` | Override the attributes of the time coordinate (`""`: the attributes; `time_units = "clock"`: clock years as they stand) |
| `time_name` | `character(len=56)` | Name of the time coordinate (the variable's last dimension) |
| `units_file` | `character(len=128)` | The `units` attribute of the variable in the (first) file, `""` without one; metadata (a caller such as [fesm_datasrc](datasrc.qmd) checks it) |

### `varslice_class`

The main object: parameters plus the loaded coordinates, time axis and data.

| Component | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `par` | `varslice_param_class` | Configuration (above) |
| `time_range(2)` | `real(dp)` | Current requested time range (set by update) |
| `slice_method` | `character(len=56)` | Current slice method (set by update) |
| `range_rep` | `integer` | Current repetition frequency (set by update) |
| `dim(:)` | `integer`, alloc. | Size of each dimension of the variable |
| `x(:)`, `y(:)`, `z(:)` | `real(wp)`, alloc. | Spatial coordinate axes |
| `time(:)`, `time_sub(:)` | `real(dp)`/`real(wp)`, alloc. | Full time axis and sub-annual index |
| `time_bnds(:,:)` | `real(dp)`, alloc. | `(2,nt)`: the CF bounds of a time axis from the file, when every file has them |
| `idx(:)` | `integer`, alloc. | Indices selected on the last update |
| `var(:,:,:,:)` | `real(wp)`, alloc. | The sliced data field `(x,y,z,time)` |

`var` is always allocated rank-4; unused trailing dimensions have size 1.

## Public API

| Procedure | Description |
|---|---|
| `varslice_init_nml` | Initialize a variable from a namelist group |
| `varslice_init_arg` | Initialize a variable from explicit arguments |
| `varslice_init_data` | (Re)load coordinates and time axis for an already-configured variable |
| `varslice_update` | Read/slice the field to match a given time or time range |
| `varslice_map_to_grid` | Remap a `varslice` field from a source grid to a target grid |
| `vs%v1(k)` / `vs%v2(k)` / `vs%v3(k)` | Type-bound natural-rank accessors: copy-return the 1-D/2-D/3-D slice at trailing index `k` (default 1), e.g. `vs%v2(m)` for `var(:,:,m,1)` |
| `varslice_get(vs, var [, k])` | Generic: a `dp` or `sp` copy of the slice at its natural rank into the caller's array (shape checked), at trailing index `k` (default 1): 0-D `var(k,1,1,1)`, 1-D `var(:,k,1,1)`, 2-D `var(:,:,k,1)`, 3-D `var(:,:,:,k)`; missing values as `mv`. Storage stays `real(wp)` |
| `varslice_nsub` | The declared sub-annual period (`time_par(4)`) |
| `varslice_sub_mean` | Mean of the current slice over its time-like axis (e.g. the sub-annual cycle), as an `(x,y,z)` field; axes the variable lacks are singleton, missing values are skipped |
| `varslice_end` | Deallocate all data arrays in the object |
| `varslice_time_decode(t, units, calendar, y [, stat])` | Calendar years `y` of the values `t` of a CF time coordinate (see *Time axis from the file*) |
| `get_matching_files` | Expand a glob pattern into a sorted list of filenames |
| `print_var_range` | Print the min/max of a field (skipping missing values) |

The types `varslice_param_class` and `varslice_class` are also public.

### Signatures

```fortran
! Initialize from a namelist group
subroutine varslice_init_nml(vs, filename, group, domain, grid_name, verbose, subs, grid, &
                             defaults_file, defaults_group, mode, remap, grid_src, time_ref)
    type(varslice_class), intent(INOUT) :: vs
    character(len=*),     intent(IN)    :: filename        ! namelist file
    character(len=*),     intent(IN)    :: group           ! namelist group name
    character(len=*),     intent(IN), optional :: domain    ! substitutes {domain}
    character(len=*),     intent(IN), optional :: grid_name ! substitutes {grid_name}
    logical,              intent(IN), optional :: verbose
    character(len=*),     intent(IN), optional :: subs(:,:) ! extra {key}->value path subs
                                                            ! subs(k,1)=key (no braces), subs(k,2)=value
    type(grid_class),     intent(IN), optional :: grid      ! target grid (remap, size check)
    character(len=*),     intent(IN), optional :: defaults_file  ! schema of the keys
    character(len=*),     intent(IN), optional :: defaults_group ! its group (default: group)
    character(len=*),     intent(IN), optional :: mode      ! overrides: auto | static | clim | transient
    character(len=*),     intent(IN), optional :: remap     ! auto | none | a map method
    character(len=*),     intent(IN), optional :: grid_src  ! grid of the file
    real(dp),             intent(IN), optional :: time_ref  ! calendar year of time zero

! Initialize from explicit arguments (no namelist)
subroutine varslice_init_arg(vs, filename, name, units_in, units_out, &
                             scale, offset, with_time, time_par)
    type(varslice_class), intent(INOUT) :: vs
    character(len=*),     intent(IN)    :: filename, name, units_in, units_out
    real(wp), optional,   intent(IN)    :: scale, offset
    logical,  optional,   intent(IN)    :: with_time
    real(dp), optional,   intent(IN)    :: time_par(:)

! Update the field to a given time or time range
subroutine varslice_update(vs, time, method, fill, rep, print_summary)
    type(varslice_class),       intent(INOUT) :: vs
    real(dp),         optional, intent(IN)    :: time(:)       ! time or [t0,t1]
    character(len=*), optional, intent(IN)    :: method        ! slice_method
    character(len=*), optional, intent(IN)    :: fill          ! none, nearest, const (overrides par%fill)
    integer,          optional, intent(IN)    :: rep           ! repetition frequency
    logical,          optional, intent(IN)    :: print_summary
```

**`method` (slice_method)** selects how the read timesteps are reduced:

- `"exact"` — the timestep matching `time` exactly (missing if unavailable).
- `"range"` — all timesteps within `[t0,t1]`, kept along the time dimension.
- `"interp"` — linear interpolation to `time` from the two bracketing
  timesteps; missing if `time` is out of bounds.
- `"extrap"` — like `"interp"`, but clamps to the first/last timestep when out
  of bounds.
- `"range_mean"`, `"range_min"`, `"range_max"`, `"range_sd"`, `"range_sum"` —
  a single slice computed as the mean / min / max / standard deviation / sum
  over `[t0,t1]`: equal weights over the samples in the closed range (both ends
  counted); it fails when none is inside.
- `"interval_mean"` — the overlap-weighted mean over `[t0,t1]` of the file's
  piecewise representation: cell means over the CF time bounds (`time_bnds`,
  when the time variable has a `bounds` attribute), else the linear
  interpolant between the samples, with partial segments at both ends. The part
  of `[t0,t1]` outside the axis holds the first or last sample. A single time
  gives the value there. With `rep = n_sub` each sub-annual step is averaged
  over the years, a year's step standing for `[year, year+1)` (so a calendar
  year gives exactly its cycle). Missing values are left out of the weights.

**`rep`** (stored as `range_rep`) is the frequency at which a range method is
applied. `rep=1` reduces the whole range to one value; `rep=12` applies the
statistic to every 12th index, yielding 12 values along the time dimension
(e.g. a monthly climatology).

**Climatologies.** Data with a sub-annual cycle but no years (`time = 0 ... nsub`,
`nsub > 1`, e.g. a monthly ocean climatology `to(x,y,depth,month)` or `t2m(x,y,month)`)
keep the cycle in their last dimension (`var(:,:,:,m)`, or `var(:,:,m,1)` without depth).
An update with `method = "range_mean"` and `rep = 1` gives the mean over the cycle; any
other update keeps it, and `varslice_sub_mean` averages it.

**`fill`** fills the missing values of the slice: `"nearest"` (value of the nearest
valid cell, per horizontal slice; a level without data takes the level above,
`fill_nearest_levels`) or `"const"` (`fill_value`). By default the group's
`fill` key (`"none"` if absent; `fill = "const"` needs `fill_value`).

The slice is read once: a later call for the same time (range), method, rep and fill
returns it as it is, and data without a time dimension is read only the first time.
Callers must not modify `vs%var`.

## Namelist configuration

`varslice_init_nml` reads the following keys from the given group (via
`nml_read` in `varslice_par_load`):

Each key bundles related quantities so the group stays short while keeping the
full provenance explicit in the file:

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `filename` | string | Source file or glob pattern; supports `{domain}`, `{grid_name}`, and any extra `{key}` tokens passed via `subs` |
| `name` | string | netCDF variable name |
| `units` | string(2) | `"<units_in>" "<units_out>"` (metadata only) |
| `scaling` | real(2) | `<unit_scale> <unit_offset>` applied on read: `value*scale + offset` |
| `time` | real(5) | `<active> <x0> <x1> <dx> <n_sub>` (see below) |
| `fill` | string | Optional: `"none"` (default), `"nearest"` or `"const"` (with `fill_value`) |
| `remap`, `grid_src` | string | Optional: read the field on its own grid `grid_src` and remap it with the kernel `remap` (`bilin`, `con`, `nn`, ...) onto the target grid given at init: a projected grid from `grid_<grid_src>.txt` next to the file (FesmData) or in `maps/`, else a lon-lat grid from the file's lon/lat |

Notes on `time = [active, x0, x1, dx, n_sub]`:

- `active` flags time-dependence: `1.0` = the variable is time-varying;
  `0.0` = the variable is static and `x0..x1` merely document the period the
  data represents (kept for provenance, never collapsed).
- `x0`, `x1`, `dx` define the file's time axis (used when `active = 1.0`); the
  generated axis must match the netCDF time length or init aborts.
- When `active = 1.0` and `dx == 0`, `x1` is forced to `x0` (single timestep).
- `n_sub` is optional (trailing) and defaults to `0`. If `n_sub > 1`, a
  sub-annual axis is built with `n_sub` steps per major unit (e.g. `n_sub = 12`
  for monthly data) and `with_time_sub` is set `.TRUE.`.

These keys unpack internally to `par%units_in/units_out`,
`par%unit_scale/unit_offset`, `par%with_time`, and `par%time_par(4)`.

An optional `mode` key (`auto`, `static`, `clim`, `transient`) states what the
variable is; with a legacy `time` key it must agree with it (`active = 1`:
transient; `0` with `n_sub > 1`: clim; else static), else init stops.

### Time axis from the file

With `time(1) < 0` (the schema default `time = -1 0 0 0 0`), or without a
`time` key, the axis is not generated from `x0, x1, dx` but read from the file:
the coordinate variable of the variable's last dimension, in every file of a
multifile set, decoded with its `units` and `calendar` attributes (or the keys
`time_units` and `calendar`), shifted by `time_ref` (`t = y - time_ref`, `y` in
calendar years), concatenated over the files and required to be strictly
increasing. Irregular axes are allowed (ICE-6G_C: 1 kyr, then 500 yr steps).
`n_sub` is inferred as the number of steps per year when every year of the
axis holds the same number of them (12 for monthly data), else 1.
`time_units = "clock"` takes the values as clock years as they stand (no
decoding, no `time_ref`).

| `units` of the time variable | Calendar year |
|---|---|
| `{seconds,minutes,hours,days} since <date>` | by `calendar`: `standard`/`gregorian` (exact day count; dates before 1582-10-15 stop), `proleptic_gregorian`, `noleap`/`365_day`, `all_leap`/`366_day`, `360_day`; year + day-of-year/days-in-year |
| `months since <date>` | `360_day` only, else stop |
| `years since <date>`, `common_years since <date>` | year of date + value |
| `yr BP`, `a BP`, `years BP`, `ka BP`, `kyr BP` | 1950 − value × {1, 1000} |
| `yr CE`, `years CE`, `AD` | value |
| `yr`, `years`, `ka` with no reference | stop: set `time_units` |

A missing `calendar` attribute means `standard` (CF). File calendars are decoded
independently of the run's calendar. `varslice_time_decode` is public.

With a file axis, `mode = "auto"` is resolved from the file: the last dimension
is a time axis if its coordinate variable is named `time`, has `axis = "T"`,
`standard_name = "time"` or decodable `units`, and a climatology if it carries
the CF `climatology` attribute (the last dimension is then the cycle, `n_sub`
its length); otherwise the variable is static. `mode = "clim"` must be explicit
for climatologies without that attribute.

### Schema (`defaults_file`)

With `defaults_file`, every key is read through the schema group
`defaults_group` of that file (`nml_read(..., defaults_file, defaults_group)`),
so a group holds only what differs from it, usually `filename` and `name`.
[fesm_datasrc](datasrc.qmd) reads its field groups this way, with the schema
`[datasrc_field]` of `par/datasrc_defaults.nml`. The keys read by varslice are
`filename`, `name`, `units`, `scaling`, `time`, `mode`, `remap`, `grid_src`,
`fill`, `fill_value`, `time_units` and `calendar`, each of which the schema must
declare. Without
`defaults_file` (the legacy path) nothing changes: `filename`, `name`, `units`,
`scaling` and `time` are required, the others optional.

The arguments `mode`, `remap`, `grid_src` and `time_ref` override the group.
`remap = "auto"` remaps with `bilin` when the grid of the file (`grid_src`, else
its global attribute `grid_name`) is known and is not the target `grid`;
otherwise the file is read as it is (and its size checked against `grid`).

Example namelist group:

```fortran
&ts_series
    filename = "input/{domain}/{grid_name}_climate.nc"
    name     = "t2m"
    units    = "K" "degC"
    scaling  = 1.0 -273.15                     ! value*scale + offset
    time     = 1.0, -22000.0, 0.0, 1.0, 12.0   ! active, x0, x1, dx, n_sub (monthly)
/
```

## Usage example

```fortran
use varslice, only : varslice_class, varslice_init_nml, varslice_update

type(varslice_class) :: vs
real(wp) :: time_now

! 1. Configure the variable from a namelist group (loads coords + time axis).
call varslice_init_nml(vs, "input_par.nml", group="ts_series", &
                       domain="Greenland", grid_name="GRL-16KM")

! 2. Update to a given time. Here: a 12-month climatology (mean over a
!    2000-year window, applied to every 12th sub-annual index).
time_now = -8000.0_wp
call varslice_update(vs, time=[time_now-1000.0_wp, time_now+1000.0_wp], &
                     method="range_mean", rep=12, print_summary=.TRUE.)

! 3. Use the result. vs%var is rank-4 (x, y, z, time); here z=1, time=1..12.
!    e.g. the January field:
!        vs%var(:,:,1,1)
!    or a single interpolated snapshot instead:
call varslice_update(vs, time=[time_now], method="interp")
!        vs%var(:,:,1,1)   ! interpolated 2-D field at time_now
```
